title: Visual-Redundancy-Controlled Parallel Decoding for Diffusion-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.25820v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Diffusion-based multimodal large language models (dMLLMs) decode by iteratively predicting tokens at multiple masked positions in parallel. This turns each decoding step into a position-selection problem: the model must choose not only which predictions are reliable in isolation, but also which positions should be committed together as context for later decoding steps. Existing confidence-based decoding ranks masked positions independently and commits the top-K positions, largely ignoring whether the committed tokens provide complementary visual grounding. We identify a step-level limitation of this strategy in multimodal settings: high-confidence tokens selected in the same step can rely on overlapping visual grounding, introducing visual redundancy among the committed tokens and leaving less complementary visual grounding available for later decoding. translated_title: 面向扩散多模态大语言模型的视觉冗余控制并行解码
translated_abstract: 基于扩散的多模态大语言模型通过在多个掩码位置并行迭代预测token来进行解码。这使得每个解码步骤变成了一个位置选择问题：模型不仅要判断哪些预测在单独来看是可靠的，还要决定哪些位置应当被一同提交作为后续解码步骤的上下文。现有的基于置信度的解码方法独立地对掩码位置进行排序并提交得分最高的K个位置，很大程度上忽略了被提交的token是否提供了互补的视觉定位信息。我们发现了该策略在多模态场景下的一个步骤级局限：同一步骤中选出的高置信度token可能依赖于相互重叠的视觉定位信息，从而在被提交的token之间引入视觉冗余，并使后续解码可用的互补视觉定位信息减少。为了量化这一效应，我们提出了视觉冗余指数（Visual Redundancy Index, VRI），它衡量……（摘要原文不完整，此处为可获得的全部内容）
tldr: 该论文发现扩散多模态大语言模型并行解码中同一步骤内被提交的高置信度token可能依赖重叠的视觉定位信息而产生视觉冗余，并提出视觉冗余指数（VRI）来量化这一效应以改进解码策略。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a step-level limitation in confidence-based parallel decoding of diffusion-based multimodal LLMs—high-confidence tokens committed in the same step can rely on overlapping visual grounding, causing visual redundancy—and introduces the Visual Redundancy Index (VRI) to quantify this effect.
